scope: Real two-tool agent with 200 entries of history and 96 pairs of notes, naturally generated final answer while another three-turn agent answers and eight incumbents stream. Same nine-worker binary and traffic generator as protected-burst. Two fresh server generations, reverse policy assignment to each of four logical cohorts.
inputs: Both real tool calls go to the busy GPU. During the wait for the second tool issue a one-token final-layout prefix preview using only history already available. Actual tool output and live tool call IDs are appended only after +650ms. Include preview and simulated tool wait in workflow time. No target retries. Byte-identical live tool IDs are not expected across fresh server generations; compare fixture hashes, logical calls, prompt lengths and cache tokens.
gates: Verify actual overlapping streams and identical logical fixture per pair. Require both tool payloads and source IDs, all three reported values, natural stop, at least 64 final tokens. Where control validates require faster workflow first and last final content; where control fails require candidate correctness and give absolute time. Protect the other reader's p95 gap and final completion and incumbent p95 gap within 5% for every matched pair. Count HTTP and validation failures. Retain stage-01 10s/18s/150ms end-user SLO. Narrow staged result is not a production default.
